title: Dicevaders is a roguelike dice-roller about overwhelming Earth's defences, coming to mobile
summary: Time to defend the Earth! Wait, no. In today's game, you're doing anything except saving the planet! Because this time around, in this follow-up to Starvaders, you play not as the saviours, but the Dicevaders, as this roguelike dice roller is set to arrive November 26th on iOS and Android! In Dicevaders, your objective is simple: overwhelm humanity's defences as you hop from planet to planet with the ultimate aim of Earth itself. To do so, you place troops onto the board, play cards and, of course, roll dice. You'll need to synergise your choices to build up combos, while deciding when to deploy your units, nudge the outcome of dice or lock the min place. Think Balatro or Dice of Kalma, mixed with destroying the Earth. ... [MORE]

title: Words With Friends picks Whimsy as its first-ever player-selected Word of the Year
summary: I was fully expecting a Gen Z word to win the Words With Friends Word of the Year. I’m technically part of that group myself, and I still couldn’t tell you what half of them mean, but that’s where I assumed things were heading. I was going to work a few of them into the opener to show willingness, but Whimsy isn’t really one for that, so that idea’s gone out the window. The community vote ran over email and social media, with Whimsy beating runner-up Iconic in the final round. Iconic doesn’t really do anything for me. Whimsy seems like a good pick, though. ... [MORE]

title: Brown is Bart Bonte's latest colour-themed micro-puzzler, out now on iOS and Android
summary: With so many big, flashy mobile games currently available to play, it can all seem a bit overwhelming. Fortunately, there's still room for fun, experimental stuff to flourish on mobile, as we've seen with solo developer Bart Bonte. Now, the latest in Bonte's series of colour-themed micro-puzzlers has just been released, with the launch of Brown for iOS and Android. If you're not familiar with Bart Bonte's previous entries such as Orange and Purple, then you'll be glad to know things are pretty straightforward. Because, rather than a core mechanic, each of the 50 levels in Bart Bonte's Brown is based around self-contained logic and puzzles, which you'll need to figure out to solve. ... [MORE]

title: Tree of Savior M, the upcoming multiplatform MMORPG from IMC Games, opens pre-registration
summary: Back in the day, the MMORPG was purely the domain of PC players, but now everyone is getting in on the action. And a dark horse candidate that's stood out for many of us is none other than Tree of Savior, IMC Games' upcoming multiplatform MMORPG that's just launched pre-registration! Tree of Savior M is set in a fantasy world where its patron goddess has vanished into the ether. Guided by divine visions, it's up to you to help safeguard the world and its people. During the course of your adventures you'll be assisted not only by the usual suite of upgrades and equipment, but also assisted by recruitable Fellows to help you out, and the pet-like Kupoles! ... title: Brawlhalla set to collaborate with My Hero Academia as Izuki Midoriya and co join the brawl
summary: Say what you like about Brawlhalla, but Ubisoft's Smash-like fighting game has chugged along quite nicely whereas other crossover-focused fighters like Multiversus have flagged. Now, Brawlhalla is reaching outside their usual crop of guest fighters to bring in the cast of none other than My Hero Academia! Each boast abilities based on their Quirks as shown in Horikoshi's hit superhero manga. ... [MORE]

title: Pokémon Go teams up with Crocs and Duolingo for a pair of crossover events
summary: A brand named after a crocodile and an app with an owl for a mascot don’t sound like natural Pokémon Go partners, though Totodile and Hoothoot might have a few things to say about that, what with Crocs avatar items out around the world from today and Duolingo’s second crossover starting on November 17th! The Crocs side is avatar items based on its Pokémon collection, and there are three of them: the Pikachu Classic Clog, the Gengar Classic Clog and the Jigglypuff Classic Platform Clog. title: Rogue Adventure offers classic, no-frills roguelike deckbuilding fun, finally on iOS
summary: Roguelike deckbuilder, roguelike deckbuilder, roguelike deckbuilder. A genre so storied that, even a few years after being invented, it recently got an entire game riffing on the title alone. But that doesn't mean it's devoid of the fun like all good trends eventually are, especially with Rogue Adventure now available on iOS! Originally released back in 2019, Rogue Adventure is a roguelike deckbuilder (see?) that has you picking from over 200 different cards as you journey across a fantasy land, doing battle with various monsters and enemies. You'll have 16 classes with different starting decks to choose from, four distinct modes and even weekly tournaments to test your mettle in. All this, and more than seven years of updates and fixes too. ... [MORE]

title: Gravemark is a roguelike dungeon crawler you can play in portrait mode, out now on iOS
summary: Ever since 1980's Rogue, the idea of venturing into a dungeon, grabbing loot and attempting to exit without being killed has thrilled hardcore players. No surprise then, that Gravemark, a portrait-mode roguelike, has really caught our eye. And now it's not just Android players able to enjoy it, as Gravemark hits iOS! At its core, Gravemark is your stereotypical roguelike. Venture into the deep dungeon, automatically battle enemies while selecting skills and potions, then decide what to put into your limited inventory space before choosing whether to plunge deeper or get out. The twists are the aforementioned auto-battles, limited inventory, and the fact you don't actually know what the loot is until you take it back to be identified. ... [MORE]

title: Lil’ Guardsman puts a twelve-year-old in charge of a fantasy kingdom's border control
summary: Lil’ Guardsman is out now on iOS and Android, and you’re playing a twelve-year-old called Lil who’s been left on gate duty. Her dad’s gone off and left her in charge, and she’s not too thrilled about it. Can’t say I blame her. Everyone who rocks up at the guard shed is her call: in, out or the dungeon. It’s border control with goblins and elves in the queue, played for laughs. You question whoever shows up, and what you say counts, and the Truth Spray and the Metal Detector help you work out who’s lying, along with a Whip, which I wasn’t expecting to see handed to a twelve-year-old. ... [MORE]

summary: Where Winds Meet and its sprawling Wuxia storyline have explored all manner of drama and action, and now you'll be faced with your toughest choices yet in their new update. As the 1st anniversary of Where Winds Meet arrives, alongside the Hutuo region, your adherence to Xia (the martial code of justice) is going to be tested like never before. The Hutuo region itself represents a dramatically different place from the far west that's been explored in previous updates. This riverside region features its own campaign that pits you against the armoured general Xiao Han, as well as exploring the idea of what Xia's true meaning is in three new storylines delving into the effects of the ongoing conflict. ... title: Minami Co. offers incremental gameplay with a maid spin and a big asterisk
summary: While we've had roguelikes, Balatro-likes and Survivors-likes all making waves on mobile, the humble incremental game remains a best-selling genre. Now, you can hop into another number-building adventure with the launch of Minami Co. for Android! Minami Co. sees you playing as Kasumi Minami, who inherits a safety pin factory from her late father. As the new CEO, it's your job to print out new pins with exciting designs and slowly grow your factory from a small workshop into a sprawling production line. Along the way, your family, consisting of your Mom and sisters Rin and Yuzu, will help further upgrade and expand until, like any good incremental game, the numbers are sky-high! ... [MORE]

title: Solitaire(ish) turns classic card stacking into a roguelike for Apple Arcade
summary: solitaire(ish) is the new one from Playstack, the publisher behind Balatro, and it’s coming to Apple Arcade next month. So, Solitaire. But a roguelike, and made in-house at Playstack Leeds. There’s a boss too, a King, and he’s allowed to change the rules on you whenever he likes (reverse stacking included, which sounds properly nasty). Most of it you’ll already know. Descending order, red on black, black on red, same as ever. Now every stack scores, though, and there’s a target to hit that keeps climbing each round. You earn cash along the way and spend it in the shop, where Switchers are the simple option, letting you swap the rank or colour of a card that’s already down. ... [MORE]

title: Loco Motive is bringing its comedy murder mystery to iOS in 2027
summary: Point-and-click adventures have always suited touchscreens, since tapping on things is most of what you do in them anyway. So, it’s good news that Loco Motive, the comedy murder mystery, is in development for iOS, with a release planned for some point in 2027. The news came out alongside the Hands On update for the PC version, which marks its second anniversary and adds full touch controls on Steam Deck. You can switch between touch, a controller and a mouse at any point, which is probably a decent sign for how it’ll play on a phone. Chucklefish says more details on the iOS version will follow. ... [MORE]

title: The Red Cathedral brings its competitive cathedral-building board game to iOS and Android
summary: It’s been a little while coming, but Devir’s digital edition of The Red Cathedral is finally out on iOS and Android (and on PC through Steam, for that matter). I wrote about it back when it was first announced in May, and Iwan had another look in September once it got a release date, so we’ve been keeping tabs on this one for most of the year. You’re after the Tsar’s favour - Ivan the Terrible, no less, and so is everyone else at the table. Up to four of you are chipping in on the same cathedral, though each of you has claimed your own bits of it, and you need to go and find the materials to actually build those bits and then decorate them. The clergy and the city’s guilds come into it too. Whoever’s racked up the most prestige by the time the whole thing is finished wins. ... [MORE]

Each year, you roll dice to work the island, harvest ingredients, combine them into recipes and then cook them down in the Scorchpot itself. title: Torchlight: Infinite brings back its permadeath server as Assassin's Creed crossover looms
summary: My first question when I heard that Torchlight: Infinite was getting an Assassin’s Creed crossover was whether anyone had thought about the practicalities. All those hooded assassins, all those monsters, and not a haystack in sight. Ubisoft's finest are going to have to improvise. The collaboration is confirmed for January 2027, with more details expected over the coming weeks.  There's something a little more immediate to get sucked into, though. The Unbound, Torchlight: Infinite's hardcore server, has returned with the arrival of SS14 Tartarus. First introduced during SS13 Afterlight last summer, it gives you a fresh start with the rather significant caveat that death is permanent. Make it through and you'll be chasing better rewards and a spot on the leaderboards. Make one mistake, and well, there's always next season. ... [MORE]

title: Warhammer Survivors reveals its roadmap, with new characters, weapons and cross-save on the way
summary: One of my colleagues gave Warhammer Survivors a go this week and lasted about a minute before a stampede of rats ran them over. The weekend has since been set aside for revenge. Good timing, because Auroch Digital has just revealed a roadmap for the Survivors-like, which is out now on iOS and Android, and there’s a lot more on the way to die to. Most of the roadmap includes free updates over the next few months, adding new characters and weapons to both the Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar halves, along with QoL fixes. Smaller patches will fill the gaps between the bigger drops, with some of them landing before the end of the year.  ... [MORE]

title: Umamusume: Pretty Derby to bring its hit concert series to the UK with new event in London
summary: With Umamusume: Pretty Derby's planned concert in Los Angeles sadly cut short earlier this year due to visa issues for performers, many of you may have resigned yourselves to one less date on the highly anticipated tour. But, for the first time ever, Umamusume: Pretty Derby's live concert is coming to Europe from January 19th to the 20th! The 7th Event World Tour: The Stage concert, taking place at the Eventim Apollo, will open ticket sales on November 17th, and features the voice talents of the Umamusume cast, performing in-character with hit songs from the popular multiplatform mobile game. Names such as Chisa Kimura (Daiwa Scarlet), Sumire Uesaka (Agnes Tachyon) and Ayaka Ohashi (Vodka). ... [MORE]
